concrete_requests: Report max_error on each track and whether it now falls below 0.06 m.
Report steering_oscillation compared with iteration 1 (0.137 to 0.165), to check whether the forward row raises jitter.
Report progress and the ended_by reason for each run, and whether any run completes the oval.
Report whether the controller needs a different kp or kd once the row sits at y = 0.05 m.
questions: Does moving the row to y = 0.05 m bring max_error below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend?
Does the forward row cause the signal to react too early, raising steering_oscillation or overshoot on the slalom?
If max_error is still above 0.06 m, is the remaining error from tracking lag or from sensing range?

intent: Test whether moving the seven-sensor row forward from y = 0.03 m to y = 0.05 m removes the max_error excess (about 0.061 m) that caused every off-track end in iteration 1, while line losses stay at zero. Other geometry is held fixed so the change can be attributed to the sensor lead. Expected result: max_error below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend, and at least one completion or substantially longer progress.
learning: Iteration 1 showed that a wider span and larger footprints remove line losses but leave a steady lateral drift of about 0.061 m. Off-track ends now come from tracking lag, not sensing dropout. The forward offset is the next lever to test.
rationale: Iteration 1 removed the line-loss problem: line_loss_events fell from 1 to 0 on all three tracks, so the wider ±0.06 m span and 16 mm footprints now keep the tape in view. The run still ends off track because max_error sits at 0.0613 m (oval), 0.0610 m (s-bend) and 0.0613 m (slalom), just over the 0.06 m limit. Progress is 0.10 to 0.21, so the robot drifts off the line without ever losing it. This matches the Integrator's rule for this case: no line losses but max_error above 0.06 m on the oval means tracking lag, so the sensor row should move forward for more lead. I therefore move the row from y = 0.03 m to y = 0.05 m and keep the seven-sensor ±0.06 m span, the 16 mm footprint and the 0.6 kg mass, since none of these is shown to be the limit. Steering oscillation rose only slightly (0.137 to 0.165 on the oval), so I keep the 16 mm footprint rather than cutting it to 12 mm. Body width stays at 0.12 m because the off-track limit is floored at 0.06 m for any body width up to 0.18 m, so it cannot be relaxed through geometry. Expected result: max_error falls below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend, which should allow at least one completed run or longer runs before off-track. If max_error stays above 0.06 m with the row at y = 0.05 m, the next step is more lead or a narrower-speed controller tune, which is the Integrator's call.
